name: David Neeld
statement:
I make murals that read as one bold image from a distance and reward a closer look, and I build them with the community that will live with them. I grew up in a Midwestern small town, so a market hall like NewBo, where neighbors, makers, and events share one roof, feels like home turf. I paint only my own designs, and I don't use AI anywhere in my work.

My most relevant comparable is Small Town, Big Heart, a 20' x 65' (1,300 sq ft) mural on the board-and-batten wall of Parkers Mercantile in downtown Liberty Hill, Texas, commissioned by the City of Liberty Hill and completed in October 2026. Its landmarks, music, dancers, and lettering came from conversations with residents and the city's committee, and I took their input through every design round. That same process fits NewBo's call to honor the district's history and how it has changed: the committee shapes the story, and I distill it into an original composition that is clear, colorful, and suitable for all ages, painted myself from start to finish. I'm glad to work around the speakers, the glass garage doors, and the stage, and to use negative space so the wall works on market days and event nights alike.

I bring 23 years as a senior engineering manager and project manager to scheduling, surface prep, and lift work. I carry $2M liability insurance, I'm 3a/3b lift certified and OSHA 10-hour trained, and I use long-lasting, professional mural materials with durable protective coatings to ensure longevity. I hold a BFA from Northern Illinois University. Other recent work includes a 9' x 23' office mural for Remote Finance Group in Fort Worth (2026), and in 2026 I was one of 8 muralists selected to paint an 8' x 8' piece live at Liberty Hill's Whimsy & Wonder festival.
